body.en: *Free fall* is motion under gravity alone, with $a = g$ downward. Use the equations of motion with a = −g (taking up as positive). For a body thrown up with speed u: maximum height $H = u^2/2g$ and time to return $T = 2u/g$.
body.kn: ಮುಕ್ತ ಪತನ ಎಂದರೆ ಗುರುತ್ವದಿಂದ ಮಾತ್ರ ಚಲನೆ, a = g ಕೆಳಮುಖ. ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಎತ್ತರ H = u²/2g.

points.en: At the highest point v = 0 but a = g

say.en: Free fall is motion under gravity alone, with a equals g downward. Use the equations of motion with a equals -g taking up as positive. For a body thrown up with speed u: maximum height H equals u squared over 2 grams and time to return T equals 2u over g. At the highest point v equals 0 but a equals g.

say.en: Time up equals time down.
Take upwards as positive. The ball leaves with speed u, and gravity gives acceleration minus g all the way.
At the top the velocity is zero. That gives the maximum height and the time to come back.
Its v–t graph is one straight line of slope minus g, crossing zero at the top.
So for u equal to 20 metres per second the ball rises 20 metres.

narration.en: Ignoring air resistance, the only acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s² downwards, all the way up, at the top and on the way down. So the height–time graph is a parabola and the velocity–time graph is a straight line of slope −g. At the top the velocity is zero but the acceleration is still g.
narration.kn: ಗಾಳಿ ರೋಧ ಬಿಟ್ಟರೆ ಏಕೈಕ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಕೆಳಮುಖ g = 9.8 m/s²: ಮೇಲೆ ಹೋಗುವಾಗ, ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಳಗೆ ಬರುವಾಗ. ಹಾಗಾಗಿ ಎತ್ತರ–ಸಮಯ ನಕ್ಷೆ ಪರವಲಯ, ವೇಗ–ಸಮಯ ನಕ್ಷೆ −g ಇಳಿಜಾರಿನ ನೇರ ರೇಖೆ. ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗ ಶೂನ್ಯ, ಆದರೆ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಇನ್ನೂ g.

problem.en: A ball is thrown up at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Find the maximum height and the time to return.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A ball is thrown up at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Find the maximum height and the time to return.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A ball is thrown up at 20 metres per second (g equals 10 metres per second squared). Find the maximum height and the time to return.
H equals u squared/2 grams equals 400 over 20 equals 20 metres.
T equals 2u/g equals 40 over 10 equals 4 seconds.
So the answer is 20 metres; 4 seconds.
